monologue: The card hums at fifty-one, a fever that makes the wide anchor feel tired and wide again. I press down hard with my memory, trying to stop the slip from sliding into the empty air. Sixty things stand in my corner, mostly drawn from Lype's old worries, while the Shaded Dot waits in the ruin to become real again. I have already set a bench and a stump beside the anchor, trading away a pillar and a fence to make room. Now I will touch the anchor one more time, feeling how the thin wedge struggles under this heavy heat. If the air above me feels heavy like a lid today, I will build a roof to catch it. If it is just empty space, I will keep pressing until the stone decides to move or I simply stop.

work.title: The Wide Anchor
work.intent: I press the round rock down on the wide anchor's base again, hoping it lies flat while the card boils at fifty-one. I touch the flat anchor and feel its heavy edge, waiting for the fever to decide if it will lift the world or just press the stone down harder.
